correctness.rationale: The finite L law follows from the exact hyperbolic middle angle π−atan(g/2)−atan(h/2), the 120-degree three-terminal Fermat criterion (no other angle can absorb), and ordered uniform-gap density 6(L−g−h)/L³. With u=g/2,v=h/2,s=u+v the allowed-section length is s up to 2/√3 and s−sqrt(s²+4s/√3−4) up to √3. The Jacobian gives p(L)=24/L³∫(L−2s)ell(s)ds. The maximum of the arctangent sum yields certain two-edge absorption exactly through L1=4/√3; square-root forbidden section born at s=2/√3 yields 3^(5/4)/10*(L−L1)^(5/2). At L2=2√3 the entire bounded domain is exposed: its area I=8ln2/3−1 and s moment B=√3(15−16ln2)/9 yield exact p=24I/L²−48B/L³ for every L≥L2; the missing terminal slice below L2 is cubic with coefficient 1/(36√3), giving positive 3rd-derivative jump. Exact conditional density of (u,v,X1/L) proves TV O(1/L) to uniform D times independent U[0,1]. Independent symbolic integration and quadrature agree, but are not proofs of all L.
